title: Twelve Days of Christmas

scenario.title: The song file is a snapshot
scenario.body: The book's tests trim the end of the output before comparing, so a song file that forgets its very last line ending still passes. A snapshot (golden-file) test compares every byte, the way diff and wc -l do: the full song is 113 lines, and the file has to say so.

character.name: Percy
character.role: a partridge who sings from a pear tree

tagline: Pick a day and Percy sings the song up to it. Every day brings one more gift, and the pile of presents keeps growing.

brain_blurbs.book: Glues the verses together and writes them out.
brain_blurbs.real: Also finishes the song with a proper last line, just like the saved copy.

rules.test_exists: Percy is in his pear tree
rules.test_usage: Explains himself when you ask for help
rules.test_one: Day one is just the partridge
rules.test_two: Day two adds two turtle doves (and "And a partridge")
rules.test_all_stdout: The whole song is 113 lines long
rules.test_all: Every day matches the saved copy, on screen and in a file
rules.test_matches_snapshot_byte_for_byte: The song file matches the saved copy exactly, down to the very last Enter
rules.test_wc_counts_113_lines: A line counter finds all 113 lines
rules.test_file_ends_with_exactly_one_newline: The file ends with one Enter: not zero, not two
rules.test_each_day_adds_one_gift: Each day has exactly one more gift than the day before
rules.test_shorter_song_is_the_start_of_the_lo: Singing 5 days gives the first 5 verses of the full song
rules.test_only_days_1_to_12: Only days 1 to 12: no "zeroth" day and no thirteenth
